summary.headline: Carraro India FY26 revenue rose 25% to INR2,255 crore and EBITDA margin reached 10.8%; FY27 growth guided at 4-12%, with West Asia risk flagged.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 37% YoY to INR606 crore, with EBITDA up 45% and margin at 11.6%, driven by strong export and domestic agri demand. For FY26, revenue rose 25% to INR2,255 crore, EBITDA rose 33% to INR2,475 million, and PAT rose 48% to INR1,306 million. Management said FY27 growth could be 4-12% depending on how the West Asia situation evolves, and it declined to restate the 100bps-a-year margin improvement target. A final dividend of INR6.75 per share was recommended.

financial_highlights.change: +45% YoY; margin vs 10.9% in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: Domestic INR14,430 million (~64%); export INR8,125 million (~36%)
Agri vehicles INR10,192 million; construction vehicles INR9,837 million

financial_highlights.change: Management estimated ~INR150 million of export incentives within it

segments.name: Agricultural vehicles (domestic 4WD axles)
segments.commentary: FY26 agri revenue INR10,192 million (+19%). Management estimates the company's domestic 4WD axle revenue grew ~30%, in line with 4WD tractor growth above 40 HP. Management estimates ~24% of the >40 HP tractor market was 4WD in FY26, and expects 40-45% in 3-5 years.

segments.name: Construction vehicles
segments.commentary: FY26 construction revenue INR9,837 million (+31%). Drivelines to Indian construction customers grew ~9% in FY26 against a ~2% domestic decline. Backhoe loader sales were positive against a ~10% BHL market decline.

segments.name: Tele Boom Handler (TBH) axles
segments.commentary: Ramp-up for a major international OEM is progressing. Management targets ~INR30 million of TBH revenue by FY29, with incremental additions of ~INR10 million and ~INR18 million over the next 2-3 years.

segments.name: Higher horsepower transmission
segments.commentary: Turkey program SOP expected in FY27; Indian customer program expected to enter production by FY28. Turkey export tractor demand is described as stabilising or softening.

segments.name: Gears and engineering services
segments.commentary: Gear business subdued in FY26; a bull gear nomination from a major OEM is worth ~INR150 million a year from FY28. Engineering services revenue was ~INR100 million in FY26, and a ~INR175 million agreement with Montra Electric is under way with prototype orders received.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth: management said 8-12% remains the target if conditions normalise, but in the current volatile environment could land at 4-8%. It stated that revenue will be positive and not decline.

FY27 EBITDA margin: management targets improvement from 10.8% but declined to give a number. It said margin will go up, will not fall below FY26 levels, and the 100bps-a-year path depends on normalisation.
FY27 capex: ~INR130 crore, close to the INR130-140 crore range, described as fully confirmed.
Revenue target of INR3,500-4,000 crore by FY30, which management said exceeds its earlier target.
Raw material localisation of ~78% in FY26, targeted at 86-88% over the next 2-3 years.
West Asia energy and supply-chain risk could hit production in H1 FY27 and extend into H2 if prolonged.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of ~INR417 million, spent on new telescopic handler axle production, high-performance transmission programs and incremental capacity.
FY27 capex plan of ~INR130-140 crore (management leaned toward INR130 crore).
Capacity is being ramped up for the medium-term 4WD demand. OEMs asked the company to keep capacity and supply chain intact.
Expansion of authorised service centres for aftermarket growth.
Company produces transmissions up to ~150 HP in India.
demand_pricing: Domestic tractor industry crossed 1 million units in FY26; the peak was ~1.2 million tractors, and industry growth is expected at 2-5%, or mid-single to mid-teens by some estimates. 4WD penetration is expected to keep rising.
Export construction orders are visible for the next six months, while export agri demand is expected to be subdued because of the Turkey downturn. US agri exports may see a slight increase.
Domestic construction is uncertain given government fertiliser subsidies. Exports grew ~32% industry-wide in FY26.
Export mix (approx.): Europe including Turkey ~50% or less, China ~8-9%, Latin America ~10%, US ~9-10%. Management cautioned these are approximate because of contract-manufacturing invoicing.

Mix was the main reason for lower Q4 gross margin: the company prioritised dispatches to customers, with cost efficiency compromised. Commodity cost pass-through lag is ~3 months under most contracts.
Labour availability has tightened, with migrant workers having left, which has pushed up labour costs.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give FY27 export outlook and FY26 revenue from the major global OEM for TBH and backhoe loader?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Rai said the TBH program is on track, with ~INR30 million of TBH revenue targeted by FY29. Backhoe export order book is 'good', but visibility is limited given geopolitical volatility.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 raw-material ratio increase was commodity inflation versus mix, and what is the pass-through lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Davide Grossi said the Q4 increase was mainly adverse product mix, not material or freight inflation. Most customer agreements pass through commodity changes over ~3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 revenue growth stay at 8-12% and how much margin expansion is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Balaji Gopalan said 8-12% is the target under normal conditions, but in the current environment it could be 4-8%. He declined to give a margin range.

qa_highlights.question: Why not repeat the 100bps-a-year margin expansion target?
qa_highlights.answer: Balaji Gopalan said guidance is hard amid disruption; margins will rise from 10.8% and will not fall, with the pace depending on how soon normalcy returns and on mix, energy and labour costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of the domestic 4WD tractor market, and what share is outsourced?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Rai estimated ~24% 4WD penetration above 40 HP in FY26 (from ~20-22%). About 60-65% of 4WD axles are outsourced and 30-35% are made in-house by OEMs; these are estimates with no formal data.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan and the FY26 export incentive within other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Davide Grossi confirmed FY27 capex of ~INR130-140 crore, more toward INR130 crore. Of ~INR285 million other income, ~INR83 million was a provision reversal and ~75% of the rest (~INR150 million) is export incentive.

qa_highlights.question: Geographic split of exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe is the largest (~50% including Turkey), with China ~8-9%, Latin America ~10% and the US ~9-10%. Management noted the split is approximate because OEMs assemble and distribute from multiple countries.

risks_watch: West Asia energy and supply-chain disruption could hit H1 FY27 production and extend into H2 if prolonged.
Margin visibility is limited: management has declined to commit to a FY27 EBITDA margin range or the 100bps annual improvement path.
Domestic construction demand depends on government spending after fertiliser subsidies. Export agri demand from Turkey is softening.
Q4 gross margin was pressured by product mix, and some customer prioritisation compromised cost efficiency.
Labour cost inflation after migrant workers left, plus energy and freight costs.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and the long-term 4WD and TBH story, but cautious and evasive on FY27 specifics: revenue growth and margin ranges were qualified as speculative, and management declined to commit to the 100bps-a-year margin path.
key_quotes: But nonetheless, I would surely say that we reached 10.8%, we will move upward, we're not going to slide backward.
We will not go back in the margins that we have reached till now.
Importantly, profitability improved in line with the guidance we had shared during the year.

adds.what: New telescopic handler (TBH) axle production line
High-performance transmission programmes (Turkey SOP expected FY27; Indian customer production by FY28)
Incremental capacity for medium-term 4WD demand (FY27 capex ~INR130-140 crore, leaning INR130 crore)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth cut to 4-8% (possibly) from 8-12%, with management calling it speculative and guaranteeing only positive revenue; FY27 capex of INR130 crore is confirmed, backed by export construction orders visible for six months and TBH/higher-HP programmes (TBH target ~INR30 million by FY29), but no specific FY27 volume or order numbers tie to the growth range.
